note: Hours and word counts are rough planning figures, not official CEFR numbers. The hour range is anchored on the US Foreign Service Institute estimate of about 1100 class hours for English speakers to reach professional working proficiency in Finnish.

stages.name: Selviytyjä
stages.milestone: Order a coffee and a korvapuusti without switching to English.
canDo: Greet people and introduce yourself
Say where you are from and where you live
Order food and drinks, ask the price
Ask where a place is and understand simple directions
grammar: Sounds, long vs short, vowel harmony
The negative verb: en, et, ei
Missä? Mistä? Mihin? (the six location cases, first look)

stages.name: Arjen sankari
stages.milestone: Book a doctor's appointment and tell the time on the phone.
canDo: Talk about family, home and daily routine
Tell the time, dates and weekdays
Describe people and things
Handle simple phone and service situations
grammar: Consonant gradation (K, P, T) as a system
Partitive after numbers and in negatives

stages.name: Kertoja
stages.milestone: Tell a friend what you did last weekend.
canDo: Talk about what happened yesterday
Give and follow instructions
Say what you think, simply
Write a short message or postcard
grammar: All six location cases with confidence

stages.name: Keskustelija
stages.milestone: Chat for ten minutes with a neighbour in the sauna.
canDo: Keep a simple conversation going
Compare things and explain preferences
Talk about experiences: 'I have been…'
Understand the main point of short announcements

stages.name: Asukas
stages.milestone: Sort out a problem at Kela, the bank or with your landlord in Finnish.
canDo: Handle routine official business
Follow everyday spoken Finnish at normal speed
Write a simple personal letter or email
Describe plans, reasons and conditions
grammar: Clauses with kun, jos, että, koska

stages.name: Itsenäinen
stages.milestone: Pass YKI level 3, the level used for Finnish citizenship.
canDo: Cope with most familiar work and social situations
Follow clear standard speech on known topics
Read everyday texts of a page or more
Write connected text about experiences and opinions

stages.name: Sujuva arjessa
stages.milestone: Watch a Finnish TV series with Finnish subtitles and follow the plot.
canDo: Join unplanned conversations on familiar topics
Explain a problem and negotiate a solution
Understand the gist of radio and TV
Tell a story with detail and feeling
grammar: Indefinite pronouns: joku, jokin, kukaan, mikään

stages.name: Ammattilainen
stages.milestone: Do a job interview in Finnish.
canDo: Work and study in Finnish
Present and defend an opinion
Follow lectures and most news
Write detailed, structured texts
grammar: Formal written style vs spoken style

stages.name: Väittelijä
stages.milestone: Read a full Finnish novel for pleasure.
canDo: Argue a case in a meeting
Understand implied meaning and humour
Read specialised texts in your own field
Write essays and reports

stages.name: Taitaja
stages.milestone: Give a prepared presentation and take questions without notes.
canDo: Speak fluently and spontaneously on many topics
Follow films, debates and fast discussion
Understand complex and literary texts
Write well-structured text in a confident style

stages.name: Mestari
stages.milestone: Read Seitsemän veljestä and laugh in the right places.
canDo: Communicate with fine shades of meaning
Understand virtually any spoken Finnish, including fast native speech
Read almost any text, old or new
Write and edit demanding texts
